If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The `cAvailableLocaleSet` field in the `LocaleUtils` class is a private static Set that has not been initialized in the constructor. This uninitialized field is used directly in the method `isAvailableLocale(Locale)`, and if `cAvailableLocaleSet` hasn't been initialized by calling `availableLocaleSet()`, a NullPointerException can occur.

Next, I will inspect the `isAvailableLocale(Locale)` method to understand how the uninitialized field `cAvailableLocaleSet` is used in this context.

messages.content: "222 :     public static boolean isAvailableLocale(Locale locale) {\n223 :         return cAvailableLocaleSet.contains(locale);\n224 :     }"

The `isAvailableLocale(Locale)` method in the `LocaleUtils` class directly uses the `cAvailableLocaleSet` field without any null check. If `cAvailableLocaleSet` is not initialized by calling `availableLocaleSet()` before this method is invoked, a NullPointerException will be thrown.

The issue reported by FindBugs regarding the uninitialized field `cAvailableLocaleSet` causing a NullPointerException in the `isAvailableLocale(Locale)` method is valid.

Next, I will suggest the best location to fix this issue.
### Diagnosis
The uninitialized `cAvailableLocaleSet` field in the `LocaleUtils` class is directly used in the `isAvailableLocale(Locale)` method without being properly initialized. This can lead to a NullPointerException when the method is called before `cAvailableLocaleSet` is initialized by `availableLocaleSet()`.

### Best Fix Locations
- `org.apache.commons.lang.LocaleUtils.<init>()`
- `org.apache.commons.lang.LocaleUtils.isAvailableLocale(java.util.Locale)`
